title: The greedy digit word and the complexity law
summary: On the greedy word w(x) of the programme's harmonic-sine construction, this paper records the factor complexity p(L) of the length-N truncation, PROVED in Lean 4 + Mathlib: the law p(L) = min(a_m+1, N-L+1) + [L <= N-a_m-1] for L >= a_m+1, the plateau a_m+2, the decay N-L+1, the maximum a_m+2 once N >= 2a_m+2, the C1 regime L+1, and A(N) = Omega_x(log log N). Six naive formulas are refuted with witnesses, p(L) = cL is impossible for any halting alphabet, and six printed statements are corrected. The matching upper bound A(N) = O(log log N) is OPEN. Not the twin prime conjecture.
recipe_md:
All commands are run from inside `research/publish/002-greedy-digit-word`. stdout carries results, stderr carries progress/timing.

1. `python3 digitword.py` -- the reference implementation of the greedy word. Expected: exit 0, every line `[OK ] L= ... p= ... (expected ..., bruteforce ...)`, ending `piecewise slopes: [...]` and `all 3.1 values reproduce: True`. Observed: exit 0.
2. `python3 rigorous_check.py` -- re-derives every ledger claim from scratch. Expected: exit 0, 31 checks, last line `ALL 31 CHECKS PASS`, no `FAIL` line; about 8 minutes.
3. `LEAN_PREFIX=$HOME/lean ./check.sh --all` -- elaborates the Lean 4 + Mathlib development (7 files, dependency order). Expected: exit 0 and one `[check] OK <file>` line per file; observed all seven OK, about 13 minutes. Requires elan at `$LEAN_PREFIX/elan` and Mathlib4 at `$LEAN_PREFIX/mathlib4`, toolchain `leanprover/lean4:v4.35.0-rc2`. Do not invoke a single module before its imports are built.
4. `python3 crosscheck.py` -- the Lean statement shapes against the Python reference. WARNING: as published this exits 1 with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'rh41'`; the script imports `rh41.rigorous_check` and the folder ships no such package. With an importable `rh41/rigorous_check.py` supplied, expected: exit 0, about 10 seconds, `all checks pass (1969905 cases examined)`.
